---
title: theme none
format:
  html:
    theme: none
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      noErrors: true
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        # `theme: none` does not suppress highlight *emission* — the
        # HTML writer still produces `hl-*` span classes around tokens.
        # What it does suppress is the default CSS that colors those
        # spans. See the prose below for the design rationale.
        - ["<pre class=\"sourceCode python\"",
           "hl-keyword\">def</span>"]
---

`theme: none` is an affirmative declaration that you're taking over
theming — typically by injecting your own stylesheets or by
JavaScript-inserted CSS nodes on the DOM. In that mode Quarto ships
only a minimal static CSS (no Bootstrap, no built-in highlight
colors): the default highlight SCSS layer is NOT included.

What this means in practice:

- `<span class="hl-keyword">` spans are still emitted around tokens,
  same as with any other theme. Highlighting is an AST-level concern
  in Quarto, not a theme-level one.
- The served CSS (under `/.quarto/project-artifacts/styles.css`)
  contains NO `.hl-*` rules. Tokens render in the surrounding text
  color — visually indistinguishable from non-highlighted code.

If you want highlight colors alongside `theme: none`, ship your own
CSS with rules like `.hl-keyword { color: green; }` via a `css:`
entry or an embedded `<style>` block.

```python
def hi():
    pass
```
